about.title: About Mortgage Calculator
about.description: The Mortgage Calculator provides comprehensive analysis of home loan payments including principal, interest, taxes, insurance, and PMI. This essential tool helps homebuyers understand the true cost of homeownership and plan their budget effectively. Calculate monthly payments, compare loan terms, and analyze the impact of down payments and interest rates to make informed decisions about one of the largest financial commitments of your lifetime.

faq.q: What does PITI stand for in mortgage calculations?
faq.a: PITI stands for Principal, Interest, Taxes, and Insurance. This represents your total monthly housing payment including the mortgage loan payment plus property taxes and homeowners insurance. Our mortgage calculator includes all PITI components for accurate payment estimates.

faq.q: How much should I put down when buying a house?
faq.a: While 20% down payment avoids PMI costs, many loan programs allow 3-5% down payments. Consider your cash flow, other debts, emergency fund needs, and long-term financial goals when deciding on down payment amount using our mortgage calculator.

faq.q: What is PMI and when can I remove it?
faq.a: PMI (Private Mortgage Insurance) is required when you put down less than 20% on a conventional loan. It can typically be removed when you reach 20% equity through mortgage payments or home value appreciation. Our calculator shows PMI costs and removal timeline.

faq.q: Should I choose a 15-year or 30-year mortgage?
faq.a: 15-year mortgages have higher monthly payments but significantly lower total interest costs. 30-year mortgages offer lower monthly payments but cost more over the loan lifetime. Use our mortgage calculator to compare both options based on your budget and financial goals.

faq.q: How do I calculate my total monthly mortgage payment?
faq.a: Your total monthly mortgage payment includes: loan principal and interest + property taxes + homeowners insurance + PMI (if applicable). Our mortgage calculator automatically computes all these components to show your complete monthly housing cost.

faq.q: What interest rate should I use in the mortgage calculator?
faq.a: Use the current mortgage interest rate quoted by your lender or the current market rate for your loan type and credit score. Rates vary based on loan term, down payment, credit score, and market conditions. Check with multiple lenders for accurate rates.
